I'm 50 this year. I only finished primary school. I've been farming these 16.9 mu for 15 years, since I came back from working construction in Shijiazhuang. My wife works three days a week at a food processing plant in town. My son is in high school. My father is 76. He can't do heavy work anymore, but he helps with spraying and watching the water.

I plant about 14 mu of cotton. The rest, almost 3 mu, I put in maize. The maize is for our own eating and for the chickens. Cotton is my main money crop. My father always grew cotton here. Some neighbors switched to wheat-maize double cropping, but I don't know that system well. Cotton pays better when the price is good.

For cotton seed, I buy the Bt hybrid from the county supply store. Costs about 90 yuan per mu. I learned my lesson six years ago — I saved my own seed that year, and the bollworm came and ate almost half my crop. Never again. I plant around April 22–25, when the soil warms up. My neighbor Lao Wang planted too early last year and had poor germination, so I wait until I see his early patch coming up okay.

For fertilizer, I put about one bag of compound fertilizer per mu as base before planting — that's about 30 kg. Then I topdress twice with urea, about half a bag per mu each time. First time is early July when the cotton flowers. Second time is mid-August when the bolls are setting. Last year fertilizer prices went up, and I tried skipping the second topdress to save money. My yield dropped by about 20 kg per mu. My cousin did the same on his farm and had the same problem. So this year I'm doing both topdresses like always. Better to spend the money than lose the yield.

I irrigate twice from my well — once at flowering, once at boll stage. Pumping costs electricity, about 60–70 yuan each time, but without water the yield drops too much. I flood irrigate because that's what my setup does.

For spraying, I put herbicide down before planting. Then insecticide four or five times over summer. Even with Bt cotton, we get aphids and spider mites. I walk the fields every few days and spray when I see bugs. The chemicals cost about 120–130 yuan per mu for the season. It's a lot, but you can't skip it.

Picking is the hard part for labor. My wife helps on weekends. My father can pick a little. But most of it is me. I'll hire women from the village for about 25 days at 100 yuan per day. That's 2,500 yuan just for hired picking. Last year I tried to do all the picking myself and lost some cotton because it got over-mature. So this year I'm hiring help.

For the maize, it's much easier. I plant the almost 3 mu in mid-April with hybrid seed, about 40 yuan per mu. I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu at planting — about 40 kg. If it gets very dry in July I might irrigate once. Otherwise maybe not. I spray herbicide once. I expect about 400 kg per mu. That's enough for our family and the chickens, maybe a little extra to sell.

My total costs this year are about 9,200 yuan. That's a lot of money. My wife brings some cash from her factory job, but the cotton is what pays for my son's school fees and any doctor bills. I'm hoping for about 230 kg of lint per mu on the cotton if the weather holds. Last year I got 220. I'm not changing much this year — with my wife working off-farm and my father getting old, I need something reliable, not experiments.
